title: Roll and Stop
hook: An empty aisle and nobody to be fast for.
scene: Painted stalls both sides, wet asphalt, the whole aisle to yourself. Nobody to beat, nobody waiting. Pick a line and see if you can stop on it.
decision: How do you move through the aisle?

options.text: Throttle, then brake at the end
options.result: You get there quickly and stop late and heavy, and both cats slide into the seat back. You arrived. You didn't stop where you meant to.

options.text: Roll, ease off early, stop on the line you picked
options.result: You let it roll, come off the throttle before you need to, and the car settles onto your line without asking anything of the brakes. Neither cat moves.

options.text: Creep the whole aisle with the brake half on
options.result: You ride it the full length. The car never settles into a roll, and you finish having fought the aisle instead of driven it.

options.text: Watch the cats and let the car find the end
options.result: You're looking at the seat when the stalls run out, so the stop isn't chosen — it's just where the paint got close.

debrief: Ease off before the stop. Smooth braking is a skill you build in a lot, before there's a street attached.

source.psdp_skill: Skill two: moving, steering, and stopping
source.teaching_target: Start, roll, and stop on a line she picked. Smooth. The cats do not slide.
